terra.problem: The passage addresses people entering through the gates, plural. It does not say they all use the same gate.
The message addresses the kings and the people of Judah and Jerusalem who enter through the gates, not necessarily everyone walking through.
The explanation broadens the address to everyone coming through, rather than the kings and the people of Judah and Jerusalem named in the passage.
The tired sandals and the end of the day add a condition and a time that the passage does not give.
Calling keeping the Sabbath holy the whole point of the day asserts a purpose the passage does not state.
The comparison to a second helping does not match the idea of a city being inhabited forever.
A parade suggests the people come together in a procession, which the passage does not say.
The explanation presents people bringing offerings from Benjamin as a present event, rather than part of the conditional promise.
The explanation presents people bringing offerings from the Negev as a present event, rather than part of the conditional promise.
